name: K-S2
description: Where the white of the far terrain in the solo pictures comes from (the owner's second symptom of 2026-11-15: the distant mountain range of the cb_far picture is a flat bright white silhouette; the baseline picture of K-S1 with every layer empty already shows it, so the cloud pass does not draw it). One start on the pad with the own cloud pass drawing (Medium, the owner's 2560x1440 at UI_SCALE 1.5, raytracing off, frame generation off, EVE removed). SurfaceProbe opens the viewer, holds the vessel and the clouds, sets the sun's elevation to 45 degrees as K-S1 does, places K-S1's cb_far pose (300 m, elevation 5, a cell 60 km ahead) and takes the same frame five times at one frozen time: old_fog (the fog rule before the package: the field's visibility is the fog's under a forced level, driver.forcedLevelOwnsFog 0), baseline (the rule now, every layer empty), drawn (the cell alone), no_weather (weatherEffects off) and no_mod (the whole mod off: Scatterer, TUFX and the game's own air only). Each frame logs 'surface: <frame>: fog ...' (RenderSettings.fog, mode, density, colour, what the fog writer holds, the weather view's level and visibility, the field's level at the vessel, the camera and the sun); the pictures are compared offline (tools/surface_frames.py): luminance, chroma and local contrast of the far terrain across the frames. The probe judges the sameness of the frames (the layer alone, the camera did not move, the sun did not move) and that each picture is written, not the look. At most 12 minutes of scenario. Rows: tests/series/rows/SURFACEPROBE.json.
